title: Increasing-cutoff stress for the Hamiltonian carre-du-champ comparison
question: Does the finite E_kin versus D_q comparison from R-402 remain two-sided when the oscillator cutoff is increased, or does the coordinate form become too small for a uniform upper comparison?

new_perspective.principle: Stress the Hamiltonian-derived comparison itself before treating its finite ratio as a candidate common-core constant.
route: Use the volume-two actual Q3 chain and increase the one-site oscillator dimension through 12.
Retain both beta values, source signs, split orders, history signs, adjoints and collar orientations while caching only exact finite prefixes.
Record minimum and maximum E_kin/D_q ratios separately at every cutoff and compare the late-cutoff profile with the d=3 baseline.
Keep the lower and upper directions separate: a finite lower ratio does not imply a uniform upper bound, and finite growth is not a divergence theorem.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: A bounded two-sided ratio would be a prerequisite for substituting D_q into the R-399 shell transfer. A growing upper ratio instead blocks that substitution while leaving a possible one-sided lower-form route open. No common-core or QFT conclusion follows either way.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks only scalar positivity and finite diagnostic arithmetic; the cutoff profile, finite matrices, likelihood rows and all limits remain in the executable/open boundary.

promotion_criteria: Replace the finite ratio profile by an analytic comparison on a cutoff-independent Hamiltonian common core.
If a one-sided comparison is pursued, prove its direction and constant separately and stress it in both phases and orientations.
Only after a valid uniform comparison may the R-399 shell transfer use the coordinate form in a regulator limit.
stop_conditions: If the upper ratio grows with cutoff, do not call the finite R-402 interval a two-sided comparison constant.
If the lower ratio collapses, do not substitute D_q for the kinetic form even one-sidedly without a new route.
Finite growth alone is not a divergence theorem; record it as a route-local stress and keep analytic uniformity open.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite cutoff stress. It proves no cutoff-independent or two-sided form comparison, no common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: A growing finite ratio profile blocks automatic extrapolation of a bounded comparison constant, but it does not prove divergence of the infinite-volume Q3 form or disprove a separately proved one-sided estimate.
